doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Comparing Basie's bands and their saxophonists
summary: Both Basie bands were great; they name tenors and Earle Warren.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: They were both great, they really were.

That other band with Prez and all of them, that was a great band. But that next one he had he was, Basie was a lucky man. ‘Cause he had some of the greatest saxophone players I believe, to come along.
First he had Lester and Herschel Evans.
Lucky Thompson. Yeah. He always had great —
He always had all these great tenors, right?
And he had a great lead alto player, Earle Warren.
People forget Earle Warren. “Smile” they used to call him. He used to smile when he played. He was great, man.
